risks: The artifact probe flags requires_gpu=true, which conflicts with the paper's single-core CPU positioning and must be investigated; a genuine GPU dependency would reduce portability.
The probe did not execute code, so build success, dataset acquisition, end-to-end commands, determinism, and benchmark duration remain unverified.
Exact subgraph counting is NP-hard, so adversarial graph-pattern pairs may cause unpredictable or excessive evaluation times unless strict workload bounds and timeouts are used.
No public-data packaging or ready-made benchmark command is established by the supplied evidence.
The repository has zero reported stars, and the recent paper has zero reported citations, so adoption and external validation are limited.
Optimizations may exploit workload-specific structure unless hidden tests deliberately vary graph size, density, degree distribution, pattern topology, and center placement.
